Corpus › Types & collections › ∈

∈

Translation status: العربية reader-locale proof. Term names and code fences follow the ar pack; supporting prose may still be English.

Checks whether a value is in a list, set, map key set, or enum value set.

Syntax: <expression> ∈ <collection> | <expression> ∉ <collection>

Category#

collection

Related#

  • ‥
  • …

Examples#

radix/corpus/operatores/membership-collection.fab (canonical · operator-group)#

Checks whether a value appears in a collection.

# =============================================================================
# ∈ — Checks whether a value appears in a collection
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Checks whether a value appears in a collection.
#   • Related operators: ‥, …
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • Using `∈` with a non-collection right operand — `∈` checks membership in a قائمة, جدول, or مجموعة (or a range), and a scalar right operand is rejected (SEM010); for a substring test on text use `contains`.
#
# See also: ‥, …
# =============================================================================

# ∈ — collection membership (element in set)
#
# <expr> ∈ <قائمة>
#
# GRAMMAR:
#   membershipExpr :← expr '∈' expr
#
# EXPECTED OUTPUT:
#   none — stdout not pinned for this exemplum.

main {
    const string condicio ← "agens"
    const int aetas ← 21

    # Basic ∈ with نص قائمة
    if condicio ∈ ["pendens", "agens", "pausa"] {
        print "condicio valida"
    }

    # ∈ with numeric قائمة
    if aetas ∈ [18, 21, 65] {
        print "aetas insignis"
    }
    print "exempla ∈"
}

radix/corpus/operatores/membership-range.fab (canonical · operator-group)#

Checks whether a value lies within a range.

# =============================================================================
# ∈ — Checks whether a value lies within a range
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Checks whether a value lies within a range.
#   • Related operators: ‥, …
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • Confusing `∈` over a range (numeric interval) with `∈` over a collection (set membership) — the right operand decides: a range such as `0‥100` tests the interval, a قائمة, جدول, or مجموعة tests membership.
#
# See also: ‥, …
# =============================================================================

# ∈ — range containment (membership in a numeric interval)
#
# <expr> ∈ <initium>‥<finis>    — half-open [initium, finis)
# <expr> ∈ <initium>…<finis>     — inclusive [initium, finis]
# <expr> ∈ <initium> before <finis> — explicit exclusive end
#
# GRAMMAR:
#   rangeMembership :← expr '∈' rangeExpr
#
# EXPECTED OUTPUT:
#   none — stdout not pinned for this exemplum.

const int aetas = 25

main {
    print "exempla ∈"

    # Basic ∈ with ‥ operator (exclusive end)
    if aetas ∈ 0‥100 {
        print "aetas intra fines est"
    }

    # ∈ with … (inclusive end)
    if aetas ∈ 18…65 {
        print "aetas laboris"
    }

    # ∈ with before (explicit exclusive)
    if aetas ∈ 0 before 18 {
        print "minor"
    }
}

radix/corpus/operatores/membership-values.fab (canonical · operator-group)#

Checks whether a value is in a list, set, map key set, or enum value set.

# =============================================================================
# ∈ — Membership over lists, sets, map keys, and enum value sets (∈ and ∉)
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • `∈` is true when the left value is in the right collection; `∉` is its negation.
#   • The right operand may be a list, a set, or a map (the test is on the keys).
#   • An enum value set is a list of enum members: `c ∈ [Color.rubrum, Color.viridis]`.
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • Using `∈` or `∉` with text on the right — they never apply to text; use `contains` for a substring test.
#   • Using `∈` with a scalar, nullable, or unresolved empty `[]` right operand — each is rejected.
#
# See also: ‥, …
# =============================================================================

# ∈ / ∉ — membership in list, set, map key, and enum value set
#
# <expr> ∈ <قائمة | مجموعة | جدول | [enum members]>
# <expr> ∉ <قائمة | مجموعة | جدول | [enum members]>
#
# GRAMMAR:
#   membershipExpr :← expr ('∈' | '∉') expr
#
# EXPECTED OUTPUT:
#   list in
#   list out
#   set in
#   set out
#   map key in
#   map key out
#   enum in
#   enum out

enum Color {
    rubrum,
    viridis,
    caeruleum
}

fn classify(Color c) → void {
    if c ∈ [Color.rubrum, Color.viridis] {
        print "enum in"
    }
    if c ∉ [Color.rubrum, Color.caeruleum] {
        print "enum out"
    }
}

main {
    # list
    const list<int> primi ← [2, 3, 5, 7]
    if 5 ∈ primi {
        print "list in"
    }
    if 4 ∉ primi {
        print "list out"
    }

    # set
    var set<string> visi ← empty
    visi.add("alpha")
    visi.add("beta")
    if "alpha" ∈ visi {
        print "set in"
    }
    if "gamma" ∉ visi {
        print "set out"
    }

    # map: the test is on the keys
    var map<string, int> puncta ← empty
    puncta["alpha"] ← 1
    puncta["beta"] ← 2
    const string present ← "beta"
    const string absent ← "gamma"
    if present ∈ puncta {
        print "map key in"
    }
    if absent ∉ puncta {
        print "map key out"
    }

    # enum value set: a list of enum members
    classify(Color.viridis)
}

Expected output:

list in
list out
set in
set out
map key in
map key out
enum in
enum out

radix/corpus/operatores/membership-decline.fab (supporting · reject)#

Membership reject harness: a scalar, nullable, unresolved empty list, text, or mixed value-set right operand is rejected.

# =============================================================================
# ∈ — membership decline (MG-6b)
# =============================================================================
# This exemplum intentionally fails to compile. The sibling .expected file
# pins only the stable diagnostic identities, not paths or rendered prose.
#
# Each statement below is one reject cell:
#   • scalar right operand            1 ∈ 5
#   • nullable collection right       n ∈ maybe
#   • unresolved empty list right     1 ∈ []
#   • mixed enum/scalar value set     c ∈ [Color.rubrum, 3]
#   • text right operand              "a" ∈ "abc" (membership never applies to
#                                     text; use contains)

enum Color {
    rubrum,
    viridis
}

fn scalar() → void {
    if 1 ∈ 5 {
        print "scalar"
    }
}

fn nullable(list<int> ∪ none maybe) → void {
    if 1 ∈ maybe {
        print "nullable"
    }
}

fn unresolved() → void {
    if 1 ∈ [] {
        print "unresolved"
    }
}

fn mixed(Color c) → void {
    if c ∈ [Color.rubrum, 3] {
        print "mixed"
    }
}

fn text() → void {
    if "a" ∈ "abc" {
        print "text"
    }
}

main {
    scalar()
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.
